back: Volume of blood pumped by one ventricle per minute = stroke volume × heart rate.
Heart rate (beats/min) = 60 ÷ duration of one cycle (s).

front: Order of events in the cardiac cycle
back: Atrial systole → ventricular systole (AV valves close, semilunar open) → diastole (semilunar close, AV open, filling).
Passively, by pressure differences: open when pressure behind is higher, close when it reverses.
SAN → atria contract → AVN delay (~0.1 s) → bundle of His → Purkyne tissue → ventricles contract from apex.

front: Why is the left ventricle wall thicker?
back: It generates higher pressure to pump blood through the whole systemic circulation.
Contracting rhythmically without nervous stimulation (cardiac muscle).
Stop atrioventricular valves turning inside out during ventricular systole.
Cardiovascular centre in the medulla (sympathetic speeds up, vagus slows) and adrenaline.
